% Notes in a revtex4-2 title block: an author's \footnote, \email, and
% \thanks, a \thanks in the title, which the PDF leaves out, and body
% footnotes after them. Eight more authors' \email notes run the marks
% past the eighth symbol, as aps's list of fifteen does. tex4ht's
% revtex4.4ht reads macros that revtex4.cls saves and revtex4-2 does not.
\documentclass{revtex4-2}
\usepackage{hyperref}
\begin{document}
\title{Revhead front\thanks{A note on the title.}}
\author{First Author\footnote{A note on the author.}}
\email{first@example.com}
\affiliation{A University}
\author{Second Author}
\thanks{A thanks of the second author.}
\affiliation{Another Institute}
\author{Author Four}
\email{four@example.com}
\author{Author Five}
\email{five@example.com}
\author{Author Six}
\email{six@example.com}
\author{Author Seven}
\email{seven@example.com}
\author{Author Eight}
\email{eight@example.com}
\author{Author Nine}
\email{nine@example.com}
\author{Author Ten}
\email{ten@example.com}
\author{Author Eleven}
\email{eleven@example.com}
\affiliation{A Third Institute}
\begin{abstract}
Text of the abstract.
\end{abstract}
\maketitle
\section{First section}
Text of the first section.\footnote{A body footnote.}
More text.\footnote{A second body footnote.}
\end{document}
